independent-reimpl.summary:
I wrote my own version of S1_ROLL100 and S2_slope3_tp60 using only the spec in the docstring (lines 1-45), without reading the tool's code. It is at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-he-thong-da-tac-tu/91ca436c-9415-5d3b-b784-e5a036caf65c/scratchpad/wf_independent-reimpl/reimpl.py and runs in about 20 s. I ran it on BTC, SOL and DOGE and compared it with two runs of the original tool. One was the run the task asked for (orig.json, 03:29 UTC), made from the uncommitted working copy and identical to the first run in intra_v1.json. The other (orig2.json) is a re-run of the version committed as 978a89b at 03:35, because the tool file changed after my first run.

S1 agrees within 0.35 % on trade count and 0.03 bps on mean net. S2 differs by about 20 % in trade count against the 03:29 run, which crosses the 20 % threshold in DEV. I traced every gap to a specific rule: adding two rules to my version reproduces each original run exactly, per symbol and per split, with mean net matching to at least 1e-6 bps.

Rule 1 (S2 only, 03:29 run): a pending S2 entry order was cancelled after 3 five-minute closes (the `pull_bars=3` parameter). This TTL appears nowhere in the spec, which says the order is re-anchored while the trend holds and cancelled only when it fails. The committed version no longer does this; on S2 it now matches my spec-literal code except for rule 2.

Rule 2 (both strategies, both runs): no new entry at a 5m close if the previous trade exited in that same minute. The spec is ambiguous here, and the effect is tiny.

So my implementation follows the spec on the S2 order lifetime, and the committed tool now does too. Neither difference changes the economic conclusion: both strategies lose about 7.5–8.5 bps per trade after costs, with win rates of 27–33 %. That is far from the user's targets of more than 50 % wins and more than +15 bps per trade.

Separately, an issue both versions share: in 89 % of S2 fills the stop from the last two closed 5m bars lands on the wrong side of the entry price. Those trades fall back to a 1×ATR stop, which is then trailed up to the low (or high) of the 5m bar the fill happened in. As a result the median S2 trade lasts only 4–5 minutes and never reaches the 45-minute time exit. If someone read the spec's "within 5 bps" rule as an absolute distance, the replay would show a fake edge.

findings.title: Shared by both versions: S2's two-bar stop is usually on the wrong side, so S2 becomes a ~5-minute trade
findings.detail: This is not a disagreement between the implementations; both behave the same way, so the spec is the issue. A long S2 entry is a buy limit at EMA20 below a close that is above EMA20. It fills when the still-open 5m bar trades down through EMA20, so the lowest low of the last two closed bars is usually above the entry price. Read as a signed distance (stop distance below 5 bps, including negative, means use 1 ATR), which is what the original's numbers match, 92 % of trades fall back to the 1×ATR stop. The stop is then trailed to the fill bar's own low at the first 5m close, which is very close to entry. That gives a median hold of 4–5 minutes and zero 45-minute time exits, so S2 does not test the request's 15–30 minute swing. Read as an absolute distance (|distance| < 5 bps), the stop often sits above the entry, and the 'in the fill minute only the stop counts' rule books those exits as profits. That produces a spurious edge. Not trailing to the fill bar does not rescue the strategy.
findings.evidence:

- Median hold: 4 min (mine), 5 min (original). Exits: 0 TIME in both.
- Absolute reading (--sl-abs): DEV n=1765, win 76.4 %, net +13.12. HOLDOUT n=660, win 82.9 %, net +16.36. This is an artefact.
- No trailing to the fill bar (--trail-skip-fill-bar): DEV n=1608, win 37.7 %, net -7.95. HOLDOUT n=620, win 37.4 %, net -8.15.
findings.direction: unclear: one alternative fix (not trailing to the fill bar) raises the win rate by about 10 percentage points but makes net slightly worse; the absolute reading would make results look falsely better
findings.suggested_fix: Say in the docstring and the report that the 5-bps fallback uses the signed distance, and that S2 trades effectively last about 5 minutes. If the 15–30 minute swing is the goal, pre-register a new stop rule, for example the last swing low before the pull-back, or wait for one closed bar before trailing. Validate it on HOLDOUT as a new variant, not as a fix to this one.

I found no look-ahead, time-alignment or leakage bug in tools/intraday_replay.py. I left the repo untouched; everything I ran is under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-he-thong-da-tac-tu/91ca436c-9415-5d3b-b784-e5a036caf65c/scratchpad/wf_lookahead-audit/.

Five independent checks support this:
(1) I re-implemented every feature with my own causal code (pandas resample, ewm, rolling, merge_asof, textbook Wilder ATR and ADX). All match the replay's values: ATR, ADX, ADX alignment and CVD exactly; EMA to about 1e-15 relative; VWAP to about 3e-10 relative.
(2) Truncating the 1m series at 5 cut points per symbol and recomputing changes no earlier feature value (max abs diff 0).
(3) I instrumented a copy of run_symbol and _exit_scan to log the time at which every price, volume and feature value it reads becomes known. Across all 18 symbol×variant runs (36,275 trades) there were 0 causality violations, and the instrumented copy reproduces the original trades bit-for-bit. Four injected one-bar look-aheads are all caught (counts in numbers).
(4) Rerunning the original pipeline, features included, on truncated data reproduces all 41,945 trades that exit before the cut, with 0 mismatches.
(5) A synthetic test shows that incomplete 5m/15m groups are dropped and that ADX falls back to the last complete 15m bar. The real data has no gaps at all, so this case never arises in the replay.

What I did find are small, non-leak timing and bookkeeping choices. Fixing them moves results by at most about +1.5 bps/trade (credible case), with an absolute upper bound of +4.8 bps/trade for S2 tp60. Break-even needs +7 to +9 bps and the request's +15 bps target needs about +22 to +24, so the negative results from the first run (S1 win rate ~32 %, net ~-8 bps; S2 win rate ~25-28 %, net ~-7 to -9 bps) are not artifacts of the simulator.

findings.title: No look-ahead in features (EMA20, slope1/3, ATR14, ADX14 on 15m, VWAP/sigma for ROLL100 and SESSION, CVD60)
findings.detail: Each feature at 5m bar k uses only 1m data up to and including the last minute of that bar. EMA slopes are causal differences. Wilder ATR and ADX are stored at the index of the bar they describe, so there is no off-by-one. ADX is taken from the last 15m bar whose close is at or before the 5m close; a 15m bar closing at the same instant is complete at that point. VWAP and sigma are read at the 5m bar's last minute, and CVD60 is 2*taker_buy_quote - quote_vol for that same minute.

findings.title: No look-ahead in simulation (fill minute, stop/target levels, trailing stop, exits, overlap)
findings.detail:
In a copy of run_symbol and _exit_scan, every read of o/h/l/c/v/qv/tbq, the b5 OHLC and the f[...] features is logged with the time it becomes known (1m bar: open+60; 5m bar: its close).

What the checks assert:
- The S1 signal uses data known at or before the 5m close tc.
- The S1 fill is evaluated only in minute i_next, which starts at tc.
- The S2 trend condition at bar kk uses data known at or before close[kk]; the fill scan starts after close[kk].
- The S2 initial stop is known at or before the fill minute's open.
- In _exit_scan, the stop and target in force at minute i are known at or before the start of minute i (the trail from the 5m bar closing at T[i]+60 applies from minute i+1).
- Bar reads never go past the current minute.
- The exit index is never before the fill index, and no trade's fill is at or before the previous trade's exit-minute close.

The fill-minute stop is path-consistent: a long limit below the open must be crossed before any low below it can print.

findings.title: S2 skips the 5m close at which a pull-back order expires, and the bar where the trend direction flips
findings.detail: The pull-back loop evaluates bars kk = k, k+1, k+2 (pull_bars = 3) and then sets k = max(k, kk) + 1 = k+4. Bar k+3's close is never evaluated as a new signal, so no order rests during the following 5 minutes even if the trend still holds. Likewise, when the loop breaks because the direction flips at kk, bar kk is not re-evaluated in the new direction. This is not a leak; it only removes trades.

A per-symbol HOLDOUT with n=1 has a degenerate bootstrap CI [x, x], so one winning trade passes. The slope1 variants clear the DEV floor (pooled DEV n=40), so if either had the best DEV mean, BTCUSDT would be marked ACTIVE-ELIGIBLE on 1 holdout trade. core/intraday_lane.py _mode() trusts config/intraday_verdict.json with no n check, so this would enable active DEMO orders. fill-cost-bounds.summary:
No. None of the bounds makes S1_ROLL100, S1_SESSION or S2_slope3_tp60 profitable after VIP0 fees, and none gets the win rate above 50%. This holds pooled and for each symbol, in DEV and in HOLDOUT.

How it was run: tools/intraday_replay.py was copied to the scratch folder as ir_orig.py, and run_symbol/_exit_scan were re-implemented with switches for each assumption. The BASE switch setting reproduces the original trade-by-trade on all 9 symbol×variant pairs (6396/5100/304 BTC, 5514/4509/1320 SOL, 5291/3889/1638 DOGE trades, every one matching).

- **(a) Optimistic bound:** touch fills, target checked before stop, TP allowed in the fill minute, time exit at maker fee. Best pooled result is S2 at -2.5 to -3.0 bps net with a 32–33% win rate. S1 stays at -5.1 to -6.6 bps with a 35–36% win rate.
- **OPT_max:** (a) plus TP filled on touch, no stop gap, and no stop check in the fill minute. It barely differs from (a): the best per-symbol win rate with VIP0 fees is 37.3%, and the best per-symbol net is -1.5 bps.
- **(b) Zero fees:** gross is about 0 for every strategy (-1.3 to +0.6 bps, CIs including or below 0), with win rates of 31–37%.
- **(a)+(b) together:** this is the only case with positive means (S2 +3.9 to +4.3 bps, S1_SESSION HOLDOUT +1.2). Even then the win rate stays at or below 38.8% pooled (41.4% for one symbol).
- **(c) Pessimistic (+1 bp on taker exits):** costs a further 0.8–0.9 bps.

So the replay is not materially too pessimistic. All the intrabar optimism together is worth about +1.6 to +2.1 bps for S1 and +5.0 to +5.9 bps for S2. The gap to break-even is 7–8.5 bps, and the gap to the user's +15 bps/trade target is more than 22 bps.

A tick-level check on real aggTrades (SOL and DOGE, September 2026, which is part of HOLDOUT) points the other way: the base model is slightly optimistic, not pessimistic. Two reasons:
- Stops fill beyond the stop level, worth +0.3 bps/trade in the bar model's favour.
- About 59–62% of S1 base fills would be rejected as post-only (GTX), because the order at the 5m close price would cross the book. The fills that survive are no better (-4.5 to -11.6 bps).

The >50% win-rate requirement also conflicts with the pre-registered geometry. S1's median target is 2.0× the stop for ROLL100 and 3.8× for SESSION, which on a random walk gives a 33% / 21% chance of hitting the target before the stop. A win rate above 50% at R:R ≥ 1.5 would need an edge of at least about +0.375R per trade. The zero-fee runs show essentially no edge.

The VIP0 round trip costs 4 bps when both sides are maker and 8 bps with a taker exit. Even a hypothetical maker 0 / taker 3 bps tier (better than any VIP0 discount) stays negative: S1 -2.2 to -3.4, S2 -2.8/-3.7. The strategies have no gross edge to protect.

htf-mean-reversion.family: HTF range mean reversion: 1-day Bollinger/VWAP bands (2-3 sigma) evaluated at 15m closes, only when ADX14(1h) < 20, target the mid band, stop 1.5-2 x ATR14(15m), max hold 4 h, maker entry at the band
htf-mean-reversion.hypothesis: The idea: when 1h trend strength is low (ADX14 on 1h < 20, a range regime), a move of 2-3 sigma away from the 1-day mean should drift back toward that mean within a few hours. Using 1-day bands instead of the replay's 100-min/5m bands makes the band-to-mid target about 150-195 bps (median, DEV), far larger than the 4-8 bps round-trip cost, so a small directional edge would survive fees. Null: touching the band says nothing about the next 4 h, so gross is about 0 and net is about minus the cost. DEV verdict: the null is not rejected. Gross is negative for all 4 variants (-4.8 to -11.2 bps/trade) and net is significantly negative for all 4 (95% CI upper bound below 0 every time).
htf-mean-reversion.literature: Bollinger (2001) "Bollinger on Bollinger Bands": defines the bands; the author himself says a band touch is not a signal on its own. Wilder (1978) "New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems": ATR and ADX; ADX < 20 is the usual "no trend" convention. Short-horizon reversal in equities, mostly explained by microstructure and liquidity provision: Lehmann (1990, QJE), Jegadeesh (1990, JF), Lo & MacKinlay (1990, RFS). Avellaneda & Lee (2010, Quant. Finance), stat-arb mean reversion: the edge decayed after costs. Brock, Lakonishok & LeBaron (1992, JF), technical rules tested before costs. Crypto intraday: Shen, Urquhart & Wang (2022, Financial Review) find Bitcoin intraday time-series momentum; Wen, Bouri, Xu & Zhao (2022, NAJEF) find a mix of momentum and reversal. Corbet & Katsiampa (2020, IRFA): asymmetric mean reversion in daily BTC returns. For this exact rule (ADX(1h)<20 + 1-day 2-3 sigma band + mid target on crypto perps at 15m with conservative maker fills): none known.

variants.name: BB2_SL2
variants.rule: Base. Bollinger mid = SMA of last 96 15m closes, sigma = their population std, K=2.0. Gate: ADX14(1h, last closed bar) < 20. At each 15m close, if flat: post-only BUY at min(lower, close) and SELL at max(upper, close), live 15 min. Fills only if a later 1m bar trades through. Skip a side whose target is < 20 bps. TP = post-only at the decision-bar mid. SL = 2.0 x ATR14(15m), taker. 240-min time exit, taker. Fees: maker 2, taker 5+1.

- BB3_SL2: -18.7 bps, Sharpe -3.0

- VW2_SL2: -12.7 bps, Sharpe -3.2

Per symbol, BB2_SL2 net:
- BTC: -9.5 bps, CI [-15.0, -3.5]
- SOL: -24.5 bps, CI [-36.8, -12.8]
- DOGE: -6.0 bps, CI [-17.1, +4.0], gross +1.2

DOGE is the least bad but is not significant. Both 2025 halves are negative for every variant. Long and short are both negative; longs are worse.

Exit mix (BB2_SL2): TP 283 trades, average gross +135; SL 742, -94; time exit 489, +47. Stops outnumber target hits about 2.6 to 1. This is why the large target-to-stop ratio (median 154 vs 88 bps) does not help.

Diagnostic, not a variant: signal-only test. This measures the sign-adjusted close-to-close forward return after a 15m close beyond the BB band with ADX(1h) < 20, with no fills and no costs.
- BTC: K=2 gives -0.1, +0.7 and +3.0 bps at 60, 120 and 240 min (standard errors 1.4-2.5).
- SOL and DOGE: negative, i.e. the move continues rather than reverting. At K=3: SOL -29 bps (se 13) and DOGE -36 bps (se 14) at 240 min.

So the band touch in an ADX<20 regime carries no reversion edge in 2025, and at 3 sigma on the altcoins it marks continuation.

Diagnostic: fill-model bound. An optimistic touch-fill version of BB2_SL2 gives -12.68 bps vs -12.87 with the trades-through rule. The fill model is not what kills this strategy; the signal is.

Spot check: the first BTC trade was hand-checked against the raw 1m bars. Band level, fill minute, stop distance and the 240-min time exit all match the 2025-01-01 data.

Limitations: funding is not modelled, as in the replay. The TP is fixed at the decision-bar mid rather than re-anchored. A 1-day rolling window can span more than a day if data has gaps.

intraday-tsmom.family: Intraday time-series momentum (session rest-of-day -> last part; rolling last-4h z-score -> next 120 min; noise-area breakout)
intraday-tsmom.hypothesis: The sign of a recent multi-hour return predicts the sign of the next 60-120 min return in BTC/SOL/DOGE USD-M perps. The return in question is either the session so far (US cash session or the UTC day) or the last 4 h. The test was whether the effect is strong enough that a maker-first entry plus a taker time exit (8-12 bps round trip at VIP0) leaves positive mean net bps per trade. Proposed mechanisms are late-informed or infrequently rebalancing traders (GHLZ 2018) and short-gamma hedging into the close (Baltussen et al. 2021). For BTC there is also my own conjecture, which is not from the literature: spot-ETF NAV hedging in the 15:00-16:00 ET reference-rate window.
intraday-tsmom.literature: These citations are from memory and I did not re-verify them in this session. Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (2018), "Market intraday momentum", JFE 129 (SPY: first half-hour predicts last half-hour). Elaut, Froemmel & Lampaert (2018), J. Financial Markets (same pattern in RUB/USD). Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens (2021), "Hedging demand and market intraday momentum", JFE 142 (rest-of-day predicts last 30 min in 60+ futures; gamma hedging). Shen, Urquhart & Wang (2022), "Bitcoin intraday time series momentum", Financial Review 57. Wen, Bouri, Xu & Zhao (2022), "Intraday return predictability in the cryptocurrency markets: momentum, reversal, or both", NAJEF (mixed results). Zarattini, Aziz & Barbon (2024), "Beat the market: an effective intraday momentum strategy for S&P500 ETF (SPY)", SSRN (noise-area breakout with VWAP trailing stop). Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012), "Time series momentum", JFE 104 (parent concept). I know of no replication on 2025-era crypto perps with maker/taker costs and through-fill execution.

Execution matches the repo replay. Decisions use closed 1m bars and act from the next minute. The post-only limit at the decision close is live for 3 minutes and fills only when price trades through it (maker 2 bps); otherwise a taker order fills at the open of minute T+3 (5 + 1 bps). Exits are taker at 6 bps. There is one position per symbol per variant, and a new decision is accepted only after the previous exit.

Holdout discipline: run_dev.py truncates the data at 2026-01-01 03:00 UTC, so I computed no 2026 result. simulate() itself has no date filter, as required.

range-breakout.family: Opening-range / session breakout (ORB): ranges set after 00:00, 08:00 and 13:30 UTC, entry needs a 5m close outside the range on 1.5x relative volume, target 1-2x the range, stop at the range middle
range-breakout.hypothesis: Liquidity and participation change at three session anchors: 00:00 UTC (daily candle and funding), 08:00 UTC (Europe open and funding) and 13:30 UTC (US cash-equity open). Information may arrive in bunches at these times. Take the range of the first 30 or 60 min after an anchor. A later closed 5m bar that closes outside that range, on quote volume at least 1.5x the same time-of-day slot's mean over the previous 20 days, would mark directional, information-driven flow. The hypothesis is that this flow continues to a 1-2x range projection before price returns to the range middle, by more than the VIP0 taker-entry costs. Null hypothesis: crypto trades 24/7 with no overnight gap or opening auction, so the session open carries no special information, and the expected net return is <= 0 after costs.

Holmberg, Lonnbark & Lundstrom (2013) Assessing the profitability of intraday opening range breakout strategies, Finance Research Letters. Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (2018) Market intraday momentum, JFE. Zarattini & Aziz (2023), ORB on QQQ, SSRN. Zarattini, Barbon & Aziz (2024) A profitable day trading strategy for the U.S. equity market, SSRN (5-min ORB with a relative-volume filter). funding-window.family: Funding-settlement window effects (00:00 / 08:00 / 16:00 UTC), conditioned on the sign of the 8h trend as a funding proxy
funding-window.hypothesis: When funding is positive (proxy: the 8h return over the funding interval is up), leveraged longs close and basis traders add perp shorts just before the snapshot. That should push price against the 8h trend in the 15-60 min before settlement. After the snapshot, payers re-open and funding collectors unwind, which should push price with the trend for 15-60 min. Negative funding is the mirror case. The prior was a drift of a few bps at most, below the 8 bps round-trip cost (maker 2 + taker 6), so NO EDGE was expected.
funding-window.literature: None of these papers tests a tradable crypto funding-settlement-window drift. I know of no peer-reviewed evidence for one. Background: He, Manela, Ross & von Wachter (2022, rev. 2024) "Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures"; Ackerer, Hugonnier & Jermann (2023/2024) "Perpetual Futures Pricing"; Christin, Routledge, Soska & Zetlin-Jones (2022/2023) "The Crypto Carry Trade". Intraday seasonality: Eross, McGroarty, Urquhart & Wolfe (2019) "The intraday dynamics of bitcoin" (RIBAF); Baur, Cahill, Godfrey & Liu (2019) Bitcoin time-of-day effects (FRL). Price pressure at fixed settlement or fixing times in other markets: Stoll & Whaley (1987) expiration-day effects (FAJ); Melvin & Prins (2015) London 4pm fix (JFM); Evans (2018) WMR fix (JBF).

volume-shock-reversal.family: Volume-shock (liquidation-cascade proxy) reversal on 1m bars: fade a bar with volume >= 5x its 60-min mean and |return| >= 3x its 60-min sigma, 50% retracement target, stop beyond the shock extreme, hold <= 60 min
volume-shock-reversal.hypothesis: In crypto perps a 1m bar with abnormal volume and an abnormal return is often forced, one-sided taker flow (stop-outs or liquidation cascades). Price-pressure theory says this non-informational flow pushes price past its efficient level, and part of the overshoot reverts once the forced flow stops, which pays whoever fades it for supplying liquidity. The counter-hypothesis is that some shocks carry information and continue, and a resting fade order gets filled exactly when the cascade keeps going (adverse selection). Pre-registered before any run (module docstring): shock defined as above using the previous 60 contiguous bars; side = -sign(r); P0 = previous close, X = shock extreme, leg = |P0-X|; TP = 50% retracement (post-only maker, fills only when traded through); SL = X - side*0.25*leg (taker + 1 bp slippage); 60 min time barrier (taker); skip if the TP is < 10 bps from the shock close. Maker entry = post-only limit at the shock close, live for 5 min, cancelled if price reaches the TP first. Taker entry = next minute's open. Execution, fees and one position per symbol are the same as tools/intraday_replay.py (ir._exit_scan).
volume-shock-reversal.literature: Grossman & Miller (1988, JF) liquidity provision and reversals; Campbell, Grossman & Wang (1993, QJE) high-volume price changes reverse more; Llorente, Michaely, Saar & Wang (2002, RFS) informed volume continues while hedging/liquidity volume reverses; Brunnermeier & Pedersen (2005, JF) predatory trading and forced-liquidation overshoot; Nagel (2012, RFS) reversal profits as liquidity-provision returns; Fung, Mok & Lam (2000, JBF) and Grant, Wolf & Yu (2005, JBF) intraday reversals after large moves in index futures; Zawadowski, Andor & Kertesz (2006, Quantitative Finance) short-term reaction after extreme 1-minute price changes. Crypto-specific 1m liquidation-cascade reversal with realistic maker/taker costs: none known.

volume-shock-reversal.notes:
RESULT: NEGATIVE. No variant is chosen. DEV is 2025-01-01..2025-12-31, pooled over BTCUSDT, SOLUSDT and DOGEUSDT with ir.summarize. All 4 pre-registered variants lose money, and the upper end of every 95% bootstrap CI is below about -6 bps/trade. The highest mean is MK_ALL at -8.17 bps, but it is negative, so the answer is NONE.

Gross edge before fees is about zero: MK_ALL -1.96, MK_L40 -2.24, TK_L40 -1.09, MK_L40_FLOW -2.14 bps. Round-trip costs are 4-12 bps, so fees decide the result.

- **Win rate:** 45-51%. TK_L40 is the only variant just above 50% (51.4%), and it still nets -11.0 bps.
- **Win and loss size:** average net win is 17-21 bps and average net loss is 29-41 bps.
- **Time-split check:** H1 and H2 of 2025 have the same sign for every variant (for example MK_L40: H1 -8.97, H2 -7.57).
- **Per symbol:** every symbol is negative in every variant. BTC is the least bad (MK_L40 -4.89 bps, CI [-8.05, -1.44]); SOL and DOGE are around -8.5 to -11.7 bps.
- **Hold time:** median hold is about 2 minutes. Almost every trade ends on SL or TP; the 60-min time barrier triggered only 0-2 times per variant.
- **Shock frequency:** shock bars in DEV were BTC 3002, SOL 2351, DOGE 2398 (about 6.4-8.2 per symbol per day). Frequency is not the problem; edge is.

Post-hoc diagnostic (DEV only, not a variant, not used for selection): average close-to-close return in the fade direction after a shock is small. At +1m it is +0.5 to +1.9 bps, which is partly bid-ask bounce. At +5m to +60m it is mixed: BTC +0.6 to +1.9, SOL +0.4 to +2.0, DOGE -2.3 to -5.4 (DOGE continues rather than reverts). Only BTC with leg >= 40 bps reached +8.1 bps at +60m (n = 466). That is about the size of the cost hurdle, comes from a post-hoc slice, and is not a basis for any change. The pre-registered stop at 0.25 x leg is tight next to post-shock 1m volatility, but no wider-stop variant was tested, by design.
